LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take

2.  SUBSTANTIAL AMENDMENT TO THE 2021-2022 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN AND
  ALHAMBRA HOME-ARP ALLOCATION PLAN – F2M20-58, N2M23-17, M2M23-31

  Assistant City Manager GARCIA delivered a staff report. This is the time and place set by
  Notice No. N2M23-17 for the City Council to hold a public hearing to consider the proposed
  Substantial Amendment to the 2021-2022 Annual Action Plan and Alhambra HOME-ARP
  Allocation Plan for activities benefiting qualifying individuals and families who are homeless,
  at risk of homelessness, or in other vulnerable populations. The City of Alhambra has been
  allocated $2,063,172 of HOME American Recovery Plan Act (HOME-ARP) funding from the
  U.S Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). For a community to receive its
  HOME-ARP allocation, the jurisdiction must develop a HOME-ARP Allocation Plan that will
  become part of the City’s 2021-22 HUD Annual Action Plan by Substantial Amendment. To
  develop Alhambra’s Draft HOME-ARP Allocation Plan, staff consulted with various
  stakeholders serving the homeless community. These are agencies that facilitate the
  Continuum of Care (CoC) in Alhambra, including homeless providers, veterans’ groups and
  public housing agencies. Consultations revealed strong support for case management;
  housing navigation; emergency, transitional, and permanent shelter; referral services;
  expedited substance abuse and mental health treatment services; and capacity-building,
  including data sharing. To address these needs within the community, the City will utilize
  HOME-ARP funds to provide homeless supportive services. The City will contract an
  experienced homeless services provider, maintain a partnership with the Los Angeles County
  Department of Mental Health, and train and develop local law enforcement personnel assigned
  to the homeless outreach team with additional training to administer outreach and field work,
  including case management and housing navigation, to address the complex needs of the
  local homeless community. The City will utilize these funds over an estimated five-year period
  for homeless support services

  Open Public Hearing:  Mayor Andrade-Stadler opened the public hearing.

  Public Comment:

  1) Lewis MCCAMMON, via Zoom, discussed the area medium income of residents and
  suggested reaching out to households with lower incomes

  Close Public Hearing:  After receiving public comment, Mayor Andrade-Stadler closed
  the public hearing.

  Discussion: Councilmember PÉREZ expressed her appreciation to staff for reaching out to
  the homeless population and offering services to them.

  Councilmember LEE expressed appreciation for the continued funding for homelessness
  services, expressed concern with income levels for renters in the City.

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER expressed appreciation for the funding received and thanked
  City commissioners for their input on this item.

  Action Taken:  After receiving public testimony, the Mayor closed the public hearing
  and, at the City Council’s discretion, approved of a Substantial Amendment to the 2021-2022
  Annual Action Plan and Alhambra HOME-ARP Allocation Plan in the amount of $2,063,172
  for activities benefiting qualifying individuals and families who are homeless, at risk of
  homelessness, or in other vulnerable populations; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-31)

3.  ACCEPT GRANT: ALHAMBRA CIVIC CENTER LIBRARY - F2M23-18, M2M23-18

  The California State Library developed the Stay & Play Grant Program to support the learning
  needs of library staff around early childhood literacy and help libraries provide spaces and
  programming to cultivate early literacy development. In November 2022, the Civic Center
  Library applied for the Stay & Play Grant Initiative and was subsequently awarded. The
  Initiative provided staff training and $4,000 to convert the Library’s Storytime Room into a Stay
  & Play early literacy learning space. The grant funds will be used to purchase literacy learning
  tools, toys and furniture that will enhance discovery and experimentation in young residents.
  Upon completion of the space transformation, the newly trained team will host 12 weeks of
  free programs for the community in late spring of 2023.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted $4,000 in grant funds from the California State
  Library to support the Library’s conversion of the Storytime Room into a Stay & Play early
  literacy learning space; appropriate revenue and expenditure funds in the amount of $4,000;
  authorized the City Manager or designee to sign the grant agreement with the California State
  Library, subject to final language approval by the City Manager and City Attorney; and, directed
  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-18)

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded:  MALONEY

6.  NIB: MAIN STREET SEWER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT BETWEEN GRANADA
  AVENUE AND EL MOLINO STREET – F2M23-26, N2M23-24

  The Main Street sewer main between Granada Avenue and El Molino Street is deficient in
  capacity. The existing 8-inch sewer pipe is expected to be surcharged during existing and
  ultimate peak wet weather conditions. The Master Plan recommends replacement of the
  existing sewer main with a larger diameter sewer main. On September 26, 2022, the City
  Council approved a contract for engineering design services from West and Associates
  Engineering Inc. to prepare plans and specifications for the project. The plans and
  specifications have been prepared and reviewed, and they are consistent with the City’s
  standards.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  qualified contractors for the Main Street Sewer Replacement Project with bids due no later
  than 10:30 a.m. on March 30, 2023, and opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

 10.  GRANT AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA AND THE SAN GABRIEL
  VALLEY MUNICIPAL WATER DISTRICT TO PURCHASE ADVANCED METER
  INFRASTRUCTURE (AMI) WATER METERS – F2M23-18, C2M23-11, M2M23-23

  The San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District (SGVMWD) provides reliable supplemental
  water for the communities of Alhambra, Azusa, Monterey Park and Sierra Madre in a cost-
  effective and environmentally responsible manner. The SGVMWD has provided its member
  agencies with financial assistance to implement programs that will increase water conservation
  and water use efficiency. The City is actively implementing the Advanced Meter Infrastructure
  (AMI) program which includes the purchase and installation of new water meters for
  residential, commercial, and irrigation users and can use the SGVMWD funds to assist with
  AMI meter purchases. The AMI meters will improve the City's ability to detect leaks, audit water
  usage, and accurately meter usage at each connection.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a Grant Agreement to receive an amount of
  $50,000.00 from the San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District to provide assistance to

14.  AUTHORIZATION TO CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE AN AMENDED AND RESTATED
  DDA FOR THE CHAPEL AVENUE AFFORDABLE HOUSING PROJECT, AS WELL AS
  VARIOUS PROJECT IMPLEMENTING DOCUMENTS – F2M20-71, M2M23-26

  On January 31, 2022 the City entered into a disposition and development agreement (“DDA”)
  for the construction of an affordable housing project on a surface parking lot adjacent to the
  City-owned parking structure on Chapel Avenue. The project proposes to build 44 affordable
  housing units on site. The Developer, Chapel Housing Partners, L.P., is planning to close on
  the property in the next few weeks. As the closing date approaches, numerous documents
  are being revised to effectuate the financing, the construction, and the affordability restrictions
  governing operation of the project. Since the Council approved the DDA, a few revisions to
  the deal points have occurred, so staff is requesting Council authorize the City Manager to
  execute final documents, consistent with the revised deal points. In addition to the changes to
  the deal structure outlined in the February 27, 2023 joint report by the Community
  Development Director and City Attorney, several implementing documents will need to be
  executed (such as lot formation documents, conveyance documents, regulatory agreements,
  etc.- but these were contemplated in the previous approved DDA.) The original DDA
  contemplated signature of these documents by the City Manager. In addition to those
  implementing documents, the City will need to execute a termination of leases for the parking
  structure that were providing security for a City bond financing that has since been repaid. To
  facilitate the closing timeline, staff is again requesting that the City Manager be authorized to
  execute these and any other implementing documents, consistent with the terms of the DDA,
  and the proposed amendments described in the February 27, 2023 joint report by the
  Community Development Director and City Attorney.

  Public Comment:

  1) Lewis MCCAMMON, via Zoom, expressed support for the project moving forward and
  stated the City should continue to conduct further outreach to non-profit organizations who
  are helping out in the project area.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the City Manager to execute an amended and
  restated disposition and development agreement with Chapel Housing Partners, L.P. as well
  as various project implementing documents. (M2M23-26)

16.  RESOLUTION AMENDING THE PERMANENT LOCAL HOUSING ALLOCATION (PLHA)
  PROGRAM – F2M20-27, R2M23-14, M2M23-28

  On July 13, 2020, under Resolution No. R2M20-28, the City Council accepted a PLHA grant,
  in an amount not to exceed $2,793,768 over five years. PLHA grant funds were made available
  in 2020 to entitlement and non-entitlement cities in California for housing-related projects and
  programs that assist in addressing the unmet housing needs of local communities. Under this
  grant, the Council directed a one-time allocation of $116,400 for the San Gabriel Valley
  Regional Housing Trust (SGVRHT), and the remaining portion of $2,677,368 was identified
  for the predevelopment, development, and acquisition of affordable rental housing in
  Alhambra-specifically, Mariposa, Chapel, and Water Lots. On December 29, 2022, the
  California Department of housing and Community Development (HCD) rejected the City’s draft
  Regulatory Agreement, which contained language subject to tenant preferences, as
  “problematic”. Funding for a Homeless Supportive/Case Management Services Program
  under PLHA is available to the City for a period of five years, through April 30, 2028. Under
  the City’s Homeless Outreach Mental Health Evaluation (HOME) Program, which includes
  partnership between the Alhambra Police Department and a Specialized Outreach Navigator,
  PLHA funds will be used to support the costs of homeless case management and supportive
  services. Due to formula allocations, the amount of funding has increased, however, to
  $2,934,464. After deducting for the SGVRHT in the amount of $116,400, the total amount of
  funds left for the homeless activity is $2,819,064.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council considered changes to the City’s Permanent Local
  Housing Allocation (PLHA) Program by rescinding Resolution No. R2M20-28 and replacing it

  the City Of Alhambra, California regarding the Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA)

  to screen and process eligible Alhambra business applications based on program guidelines
  and other requirements for the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).
  An amendment to Ms. Luna’s contract is currently necessary to ensure continued SBAG
  Program delivery through December 31, 2023. Program Delivery costs are covered under the
  City’s CDBG-CV funds.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council approved an amendment, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to Contract No. K2M20-335 between Esther

  to exceed $75,000; authorized the City Manager to execute the Amendment; and, directed
  staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M23-29)

20.  RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING A PROCESSING FEE FOR THE ISSUANCE OF
  CONCEALED CARRY WEAPON (CCW) PERMITS; AUTHORIZE AN AGREEMENT FOR
  CCW PROCESSING AND APPROPRIATE FUNDS FOR SERVICE IMPLEMENTATION –
  F2M23-28, R2M23-7, C2M23-12, M2M23-32

  Historically, the Los Angeles County Sherrif’s Department processed and issued all CCW
  permits within Los Angeles County. Effective August 1, 2022, the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
  Department is no longer accepting applications from residents living within municipalities not
  served by the Sheriff’s Department. The Alhambra Police Department will assume the
  responsibility for the issuance of CCW permits to the residents of Alhambra. The process
  includes an application, interview, psychological review, training, gun inspection and
  proficiency examination, among other details. To support the processing of the CCW permit
  requirements, the Police Department is requesting to enter into an agreement with MPI, Inc.,
  MyCCW.us, which provide Police Officer Standards and Training (POST) certified background
  11
2-27-23
   investigators, document collection and notifications to applicants. Additionally, there are
  several applicant fees associated with the processing of a CCW and the California Penal Code
  allows cities to charge fees to offset the cost of CCW license issuance. Therefore, staff
  requests that the City Council adopt a resolution to establish administrative fees for the
  issuance of CCW permits and add those fees to the City’s Fee Schedule. Finally, staff requests
  an expenditure appropriation of $15,000 for the implementation of CCW permit processing
  services.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M23-7 entitled: A Resolution

24.  RESTRUCTURING OF THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE: ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION
  APPROVING A CLASS SPECIFICATION FOR SENIOR ACCOUNTANT AND ADOPTION
  OF AN URGENCY ORDINANCE AMENDING ORDINANCE NO. O2M23-4809 RELATING
  TO THE POSITION OF SENIOR ACCOUNTANT IN THE FINANCE DEPARTMENT –
  F2M23-2, R2M23-11, O2M23-4810, M2M23-33

  The Finance Department recently experienced two vacancies due to the retirement of a Senior
  Account Clerk and resignation of an Accounting Manager. This creates opportunity to examine
  the existing staffing structure, operations and functions, and customer service. After two failed
  recruitments for an Accounting Manager, staff has determined the need to replace the position
  with a Senior Accountant position. The Senior Accountant position will require less supervisory
  experience, but will still provide a high level of technical and complex financial support to the
  Finance Director, while providing supervision to staff in the Accounting Division. The Senior
  Account Clerk, who performed Accounts Receivables billing of false alarms, damage to City
  property, and other billing, recently retired. Staff is requesting to eliminate the budget funding
  and appropriation for the Senior Account Clerk position and reappropriate said funding to
  create an Account Clerk position, which will result in a cost savings. With the cost savings,
  staff is requesting to fund one additional Account Clerk for the Payroll Division to provide
  additional support. Staff will also eliminate the budget funding for one full-time Cashier I
  position to fund the additional full-time Account Clerk. Additionally, Alhambra Municipal Code
  Section 2.48.070 (B) provides that before a class specification becomes effective or other
  changes are made to the City’s Classification Plan, it shall first be approved by the City Council.
  Therefore, staff recommends that the City Council adopt a resolution approving the class
  specification for the Senior Accountant position. An urgency ordinance memorializing these
  changes is necessary in order to allow for the immediate recruitment of the new classification
  of Senior Accountant and to provide the Finance Department with the much-needed expertise
  and support necessary.

  Discussion:  None

  Action Taken:  City Council, by one motion, took the following actions: 1) Approved
  the restructuring of the Department of Finance by eliminating the budget appropriation for one
  full-time Cashier I, one full-time Senior Account Clerk, and one full-time Accounting Manager
  and reallocating said appropriations to fund one full-time Senior Accountant and two full-time
  Account Clerk positions; 2) Adopted Resolution No. R2M23-11 entitled: A Resolution of the
  Alhambra City Council approving a class specification for Senior Accountant; 3) Directed the
  City Attorney to introduce and give reading by title only, waiving further reading to the following
  urgency ordinance entitled:
